metadata.title: Causal Couture — Phase 4 Architecture Preparation
metadata.historical_scope: Week 4 analytical and backend architecture preparation only
metadata.continuity: Direct continuation of the Causal Couture Week 3 video; no Week X of 4 badge or persistent series label.
metadata.methodological_boundary: Observed signals describe uploaded-data patterns; scenario simulations are user-driven hypotheticals and not forecasts; causal effects require separate causal-inference methodology.
metadata.production_gate: Narration and pacing approved; visual rendering authorized.

beats.narration_text: Week 3 ended with the Scenario Intelligence framework, user experience, and modular backend direction designed. The next step was preparing the analytical and backend architecture required for Phase 4 implementation.

shot.visual_intent: Continue directly from Week 3's Prepared for Implementation outcome into a Phase 4 architecture blueprint.

beats.narration_text: I reviewed how the existing Phase 3 analytical logic would support several downstream capabilities. The central architectural goal was to reuse the underlying calculations instead of duplicating them across the application.

shot.visual_intent: Consolidate faint duplicated calculation blocks into a planned shared analytical layer.

beats.narration_text: The existing business scorecard evaluated four analytical dimensions: Demand Pressure, Stock Risk, Engagement Momentum, and Conversion Strength. These remained the foundation of the planned Phase 4 intelligence layer.

shot.visual_intent: Reintroduce the four existing scorecard dimensions without values.

beats.narration_text: The four dimensions feed an Overall Signal, which is then translated into a business recommendation. This established scorecard-to-recommendation flow needed to remain consistent as the platform expanded.

shot.visual_intent: Four scorecards converge into Overall Signal and Business Recommendation with no formulas or outputs.

beats.narration_text: I planned a more modular scorecard structure in which each analytical signal could be calculated independently. Separating the components would make the same signals available to different parts of the platform.

shot.visual_intent: Separate each score dimension into an independently calculated planned module.

beats.narration_text: This included defining reusable analytical functions for the individual score components. Instead of rebuilding a calculation for every feature, downstream components could rely on the same analytical foundation.

shot.visual_intent: Reusable score components feed several planned downstream consumers without code or invented function names.

beats.narration_text: I also established a consistent zero-to-one-hundred scoring structure. The shared range would allow the different analytical outputs to be compared and presented consistently, without changing their individual responsibilities.

shot.visual_intent: Four empty score rails share zero and one hundred endpoints with no values, markers, or thresholds.

beats.narration_text: The recommendation layer also needed more structure. Rather than returning only plain text, I defined a consistent output organized as Action, Priority, Confidence, and Reason.

shot.visual_intent: Reorganize a generic text response into the four defined recommendation fields.

beats.narration_text: The eventual system could distinguish between action categories such as Reorder, Monitor, Hold, and Deprioritize. These were defined as possible structured outputs, not as observed recommendations from this period.

shot.visual_intent: Four equal planned action category cards with no triggers, thresholds, or results.

beats.narration_text: A structured recommendation could later be consumed consistently by the dashboard, scenario analysis, alerts, and the frontend. Each component could interpret the same fields without inventing its own recommendation format.

shot.visual_intent: The recommendation structure branches into four explicitly planned consumer components.

beats.narration_text: The analytical functions also needed defensive handling for missing or non-numeric values. This was important because small or incomplete fashion-business datasets should not make the analytical workflow unstable.

shot.visual_intent: Abstract incomplete data passes through a defensive-handling boundary without invented fallback rules.

beats.narration_text: I organized the planned Phase 4 architecture around five responsibilities: Core Analytics, Scenario Intelligence, Trend Intelligence, Alert Intelligence, and Dashboard Aggregation.

shot.visual_intent: Five planned responsibility modules with Core Analytics as the shared foundation.

beats.narration_text: Core Analytics would provide reusable baseline scores and recommendation logic. The other components would apply hypothetical changes, evaluate period-to-period patterns, identify signal combinations requiring attention, and aggregate the results for the frontend.

shot.visual_intent: Spotlight only the component responsibilities stated in the report.

beats.narration_text: These components depend on some of the same calculations. The architecture therefore used a shared analytical layer instead of implementing separate versions of the scorecard for the dashboard and Scenario Lab.

shot.visual_intent: One shared Core Analytics layer branches into Dashboard and Scenario Lab workflows.

beats.narration_text: The input to this architecture remained the existing unified date-by-SKU dataset. That dataset would feed Core Analytics before its signals were used by the planned Phase 4 intelligence components.

shot.visual_intent: Generated date-by-SKU dataset abstraction feeds Core Analytics; no fabricated rows or identifiers.

beats.narration_text: The intended flow became: Unified Dataset, Core Analytics, Trends, Alerts, and Scenario Analysis, then Dashboard, and finally Business Decision.

shot.visual_intent: Full intended analytical flow with trends, alerts, and scenario analysis in a parallel middle tier.

beats.narration_text: This approach preserved the Phase 1 through Phase 3 ingestion and preprocessing pipeline. Phase 4 would add a new intelligence layer on top of the unified dataset rather than rebuilding the existing data foundation.

shot.visual_intent: Preserved ingestion and preprocessing form the lower layer beneath a planned intelligence layer.

beats.narration_text: The methodological boundaries also remained explicit. Observed signals describe patterns in uploaded data. Scenario simulations are user-driven hypothetical changes. Causal effects require a separate causal-inference methodology and are not produced by this architecture.

shot.visual_intent: Three-lane boundary separates observed patterns, user hypotheticals, and causal effects requiring separate methodology.

beats.narration_text: By the end of Week 4, the analytical and backend architecture for Phase 4 had been prepared: a modular scorecard, structured recommendations, defined component responsibilities, and an integration path from the unified dataset into scenario, trend, alert, and dashboard layers. I’m Ushasvi Rachel, for Humanitarians.ai.

shot.visual_intent: Close on architecture preparation with presenter and organization branding; no week counter.
